short: DTW pseudo targets (M02) follow prior EMG target transfer; the mode discriminator (M03) is untested by its ablation; silent MCD/STOI use self-made references and 18 speakers are dropped.
position: The paper [@zheng2023pseudo] changes the silent training target (M02) and adds joint silent-vocalized training with a speaking-mode discriminator (M03); both are standard. DTW transfer of vocalized targets to silent articulation was established for silent EMG [@janke2017emg], with realignment by the partially trained model [@gaddy2020digital]; neither is cited. The read priors aim domain-adversarial training at speakers or sessions [@wand2017lipreading; @wand2018session], so the speaking-mode label is new, but its single-run ablation drops the vocalized loss with the discriminator. Silent MCD and STOI are scored against the method's own vocoded pseudo targets, and 18 of 81 speakers were dropped from the silent test by the same DTW cost (Sec. 4.2). The silent WER gain (59.960% to 43.114%, Table 1) is relatively smaller than the vocalized gain (28% against 36%); the absolute silent-vocalized gap narrows by 7.3 points, but the ratio widens from 2.2 to 2.5 (inference).
